title: GraphSAGE
interviewAnswer: GraphSAGE learns aggregation functions that combine sampled neighbor features, enabling inductive embeddings for nodes that were not present during training.
why: GraphSAGE is a key inductive GNN architecture and directly supports reviewer/recommendation systems where new nodes appear over time.
intuition: Instead of learning one embedding per node, GraphSAGE learns how to combine a node’s features with sampled neighbor features. That learned aggregator can be applied to unseen nodes.
deepDive: At each layer, sample/aggregate neighbor representations and combine them with the node’s current representation, often followed by nonlinear transformation/normalization. Mean, pooling and LSTM-style aggregators are possible. Sampling makes training scalable on large graphs, while inductive parameter sharing allows embeddings for new nodes if their features/neighborhood are available.
workedExample: For a new PR, its CodeBERT features plus learned transformations/graph context can place it near developers with relevant historical expertise without retraining a free embedding for that exact PR node.
code:
# Conceptual PyG layer
from torch_geometric.nn import SAGEConv
conv=SAGEConv(in_channels=768,out_channels=768)
commonMistakes: Saying GraphSAGE requires every test node to exist during training.
Confusing graph structure with text similarity alone.
followUps: How do you handle no-neighbor cold-start nodes?
How do you use it for link prediction?
production: Refresh graph edges/features incrementally, bound neighbor sampling for latency, monitor cold-start quality and separate candidate generation from final ranking/business constraints.

lab.goal: Implement one GraphSAGE-style neighbor aggregation step with mean aggregation.
lab.buildIt:
import numpy as np
X=np.array([[1.,0.],[0.,1.],[1.,1.]])
neighbors={0:[1,2],1:[0],2:[0]}
out=[]
for i in range(len(X)):
    agg=X[neighbors[i]].mean(0)
    out.append(np.concatenate([X[i],agg]))
out=np.stack(out)
print(out)
